SQLite amalgamation vendored for Qenome
=======================================

                 sqlite3expert extension (ext/expert: sqlite3expert.c + .h)
Version        : 3.53.4

Release date   : 2026-07-24
Vendored files : sqlite3.c, sqlite3.h, sqlite3expert.c, sqlite3expert.h. The
                 zip also contains shell.c and sqlite3ext.h; the shell and the
                 extension header are not vendored.

Verification
------------
Official published SHA3-256 for sqlite3.c of version 3.53.4 (release log):
  https://sqlite.org/releaselog/3_53_4.html
  SHA3-256 for sqlite3.c: 67f423e9ebbbdc473cbc4772c872ee6b89f31fde4ed0279a5c25d5f65c043a16

Measured SHA3-256 of the published files, before the row-count patch
(python3 hashlib.sha3_256 and `openssl dgst -sha3-256` agree):
  sqlite3.c : 67f423e9ebbbdc473cbc4772c872ee6b89f31fde4ed0279a5c25d5f65c043a16  (matches the official value above)
  sqlite3.h : 89d0de498b1012938bb78dc18b68fea52e26f7f7b6db6347d126a2e58b86a05c
  zip       : 628a44cfe82c66aed1ccbbe85a562d2e33ebe64b3288981ed76285612227934e
The vendored sqlite3.c / sqlite3.h are these files with the patch below applied,
so they no longer match these values; their SHA-256 is recorded under "Patched
file hashes" below.

Where the official value comes from:
- sqlite.org publishes SHA3-256 hashes for the *current* release on
  https://sqlite.org/download.html. For releases that are no longer current it
  publishes the hash of the amalgamated sqlite3.c in the release log instead.
  The zip-level hash of 3.53.4 is not published by sqlite.org.
- The SQLITE_SOURCE_ID in the vendored sqlite3.c / sqlite3.h matches the value
  in the same release log entry and the check-in shown on
  https://sqlite.org/chronology.html (bf7c7f30, 2026-07-24).

How to re-verify
----------------
  curl -O https://sqlite.org/2026/sqlite-amalgamation-3530400.zip
  openssl dgst -sha3-256 sqlite-amalgamation-3530400.zip
  unzip -j sqlite-amalgamation-3530400.zip \
      sqlite-amalgamation-3530400/sqlite3.c sqlite-amalgamation-3530400/sqlite3.h -d /tmp/sqlite-check
  openssl dgst -sha3-256 /tmp/sqlite-check/sqlite3.c   # compare with the official value above
  openssl dgst -sha3-256 /tmp/sqlite-check/sqlite3.h
  python3 scripts/apply_sqlite_row_counts_patch.py \
      --source /tmp/sqlite-check --output /tmp/sqlite-patched
  # compare /tmp/sqlite-patched/* with vendor/sqlite3 (SHA-256 under "Patched
  # file hashes" below), or simply diff them.

License / origin
----------------
Public domain ("SQLite Blessing"): https://sqlite.org/copyright.html
The amalgamation is the official build product of the SQLite source at the
check-in above. Do not edit these files by hand. The only change Qenome makes to
them is the row-count patch below, applied by
scripts/apply_sqlite_row_counts_patch.py. To update the pinned release, repeat
the steps above, re-apply the patch, and record the new release, hashes, and
source id here plus the constants in src/sqlite.zig.

sqlite3expert (vendor/sqlite3/sqlite3expert.c and sqlite3expert.h)
-------------------------------------------------------------------
Qenome --suggest runs SQLite's one-index advisor. These two files are part of
the SQLite source tree (ext/expert/) at the same check-in as the amalgamation
above; they are not part of the amalgamation zip and are stored unmodified.

Updating
--------
The expert files carry no version check of their own, and nothing compares them
with sqlite.zig's pinned_source_id at run time. When the pinned SQLite changes,
fetch both files from the new check-in, update this section, and rebuild. A pair
that does not match the check-in build is not detected automatically; this
record and the build are the check.

Guard in Qenome
---------------
--suggest does not trust the expert with an arbitrary schema. Before the
expert runs, src/cli/suggest.zig checks every sqlite_schema row: it must be one
plain CREATE TABLE / INDEX / UNIQUE INDEX / VIEW / TRIGGER / VIRTUAL TABLE
statement and must not use the expert virtual table. While the expert runs, a
sqlite3_auto_extension initializer guards the connections it opens: it denies
SQLITE_ATTACH and SQLITE_DETACH, allows only the index_list and index_xinfo
PRAGMAs, and sets SQLITE_LIMIT_ATTACHED to 0. After sqlite3_expert_new the
expert installs its own authorizer on its analysis copy (dbv); the attached
database limit stays in force there. The guard is cancelled after
sqlite3_expert_destroy, and a registration failure stops the run before the
expert is called.

When SQLite or these expert files are updated, re-read
ext/expert/sqlite3expert.c for new PRAGMA use, ATTACH / DETACH, VACUUM INTO, or
other file access, and update the allowlist and the preflight together. The
preflight is the primary defence; the guard is the second layer. The guard is
an authorizer deny list plus a PRAGMA allow list, so a future SQLite that adds
another way to touch a file needs a review here.

Row-count patch
---------------
Qenome reports how many rows each copy read and wrote. Those counters are not
part of SQLite 3.53.4, so the amalgamation is built with Cloudflare's patch from
workerd, which is the same counter a local D1 database reports.

Patch file     : patches/0001-row-counts-plain.patch (stored unmodified)
Upstream       : https://github.com/cloudflare/workerd
Upstream path  : patches/sqlite/0001-row-counts-plain.patch
Upstream commit: ddfde6c8f3d611e31cdca8c17ca8e31eafda077b (2026-08-21)
Fetched (UTC)  : 2026-10-26T15:18:00Z
Fetched from   : https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cloudflare/workerd/ddfde6c8f3d611e31cdca8c17ca8e31eafda077b/patches/sqlite/0001-row-counts-plain.patch
SHA-256        : ffafcb374b0f433964fec75d79cb5e690aa3fbe8c0df3d0a9413001deda3951c
License        : Apache-2.0 (workerd); the counters are the libSQL extension,
                 MIT (Copyright 2023 the sqld authors). See NOTICE at the
                 repository root.

What it changes
---------------
It adds two counters to sqlite3_stmt_status():
  LIBSQL_STMTSTATUS_BASE          = 1024
  LIBSQL_STMTSTATUS_ROWS_READ     = 1025  (OP_Count, OP_Seek*, OP_NotExists,
                                           OP_SeekRowid, OP_Last, OP_Rewind,
                                           OP_Next, OP_VNext)
  LIBSQL_STMTSTATUS_ROWS_WRITTEN  = 1026  (OP_Insert, OP_IdxInsert, OP_Delete,
                                           OP_Clear, OP_VUpdate, skipping
                                           ephemeral cursors)
The storage is the new `u32 aLibsqlCounter[3]` field in Vdbe.

Applied hunks and the one amalgamation difference
-------------------------------------------------
The patch is written against the plain source, so its six file sections carry
`sqlite-src-pristine/src/<file>` paths. Four of them concern the vendored files;
the fifth, `src/shell.c.in`, is dropped because the shell is not vendored:

  src/vdbe.c        -> sqlite3.c  12 hunks added a counter step
  src/vdbeInt.h     -> sqlite3.c   1 hunk adds the array field
  src/vdbeapi.c     -> sqlite3.c   2 hunks (bounds check, read/write branch)
  src/sqlite.h.in   -> sqlite3.c and sqlite3.h  (2 hunks add the constants)
  src/shell.c.in    -> not vendored

With zero fuzz, 14 of the 15 applied hunks match the amalgamation exactly. The
remaining one, the SQLITE_ENABLE_API_ARMOR bounds check in sqlite3_stmt_status,
has the plain source line

  int sqlite3_stmt_status(sqlite3_stmt *pStmt, int op, int resetFlag){

as its first context line, while the amalgamation generator
(tool/mksqlite3c.tcl, `set line SQLITE_API`) writes

  SQLITE_API int sqlite3_stmt_status(sqlite3_stmt *pStmt, int op, int resetFlag){

so the context line differs by that decoration. The script accepts this single
line as a declared substitute and still requires every other line of every hunk
to match; it fails loudly on any other difference, on a line that matches twice,
and on a patch or input whose hash differs from the ones recorded here. No line
of the patch is skipped, and the changed lines are exactly the patch's.

How to re-apply
---------------
  curl -O https://sqlite.org/2026/sqlite-amalgamation-3530400.zip
  unzip -j sqlite-amalgamation-3530400.zip \
      sqlite-amalgamation-3530400/sqlite3.c sqlite-amalgamation-3530400/sqlite3.h -d /tmp/sqlite-pristine
  python3 scripts/apply_sqlite_row_counts_patch.py \
      --source /tmp/sqlite-pristine --output vendor/sqlite3

The script checks the SHA3-256 of both inputs against the published ones above,
prints the SHA-256 of the two outputs, and needs only python3 (no patch command),
so it runs on Linux, macOS, and Windows. CI does not run it; it is the recipe for
updating the vendored SQLite.

Patched file hashes (SHA-256, after the patch)
---------------------------------------------
  sqlite3.c : ce050329ef7d8337ca050787a4c154d07561206967e54e4c01cbc3804cab56ef
  sqlite3.h : 1cef3e2dc82f1b5b603bcd6f8fe2434d421369b8c98ef9549a182294270eea6d

Calling sqlite3_stmt_status
---------------------------
The counters live in an array of three u32 next to the statement's other
counters, and the patch only bounds-checks the opcode when
SQLITE_ENABLE_API_ARMOR is compiled in, which this build does not. Pass only
LIBSQL_STMTSTATUS_ROWS_READ and LIBSQL_STMTSTATUS_ROWS_WRITTEN (the constants in
src/sqlite.zig); any other value of 1024 or above reads past the array.

The array holds u32 values and the patch does not widen them, so each counter
counts modulo 4294967296 and wraps silently past that point. src/db.zig reports
the value it reads, without wrap detection, so a statement that reads more than
4294967295 rows in one execution reports a wrapped number; a cross join reaches
that with rows in the millions and --timeout-ms 0. The older counters
(vm_steps, fullscan_steps) wrap the same way and were never detected either.

Compile flags (kept in sync with build.zig)
-------------------------------------------
  -DSQLITE_THREADSAFE=0         single-threaded CLI, no mutexing
  -DSQLITE_OMIT_LOAD_EXTENSION  no loadable extensions
  -DNDEBUG                      no C assertions (release behaviour)
  -fwrapv                       signed integer overflow wraps instead of
                                trapping. Zig compiles C with overflow
                                checks, but SQLite's code assumes wrapping
                                (for example the aggregate step counter at
                                sqlite3.c:104523, which backs the deprecated
                                sqlite3_aggregate_count()). Without this
                                flag an aggregate stepped more than 2^31
                                times aborts the process (SIGABRT, exit 134)
                                instead of returning a documented exit code
                                (D-106). It applies to the whole vendored
                                file: other signed add/sub/mul overflows in
                                it also stop trapping, while zero-division,
                                shift and pointer checks stay enabled. Do not
                                remove it without re-reading D-106 in the
                                working plan/TODO.

Note: the version string of the SQLite CLI installed on the development machine
(3.51.2 ... cbalt1) is a different build product and is older than this
amalgamation; the vendored amalgamation reports the source id above.
